arguments.content:
# Slack Web API Reference

Table of contents:
- [Authentication and tokens](#authentication-and-tokens)
- [Calling conventions](#calling-conventions)
- [Endpoint catalog](#endpoint-catalog)
- [Channel names vs. IDs](#channel-names-vs-ids)
- [Timestamps](#timestamps)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Rate limits](#rate-limits)
- [Error handling](#error-handling)

## Authentication and tokens

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/`; every method is an HTTP POST with form-encoded or JSON body.
- Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`. Bot tokens can only act where the bot app is installed (visible channels only).
- Incoming webhooks (URLs starting `https://hooks.slack.com/services/`) post to one channel without a token and only support sending messages.
- Store tokens in environment variables (`SLACK_TOKEN`, `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`). Never hardcode or print them.

## Calling conventions

- Every response contains `"ok": true|false`. Always check it — HTTP 200 does not imply success.
- On failure, response includes `"error"` with a machine-readable reason such as `not_in_channel`, `invalid_auth`, `missing_scope`, `ratelimited`, `channel_not_found`.
- Use `slack-api/scripts/slack_api.py` for calls; it sets auth from `SLACK_TOKEN`, parses values, and merges paginated results with `--paginate`.

## Endpoint catalog

Common endpoints and the scopes they need (bot-token scopes shown; user-token equivalents exist for most).

| Purpose | Method | Key params | Required scopes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Test auth | `auth.test` | — | none |
| Send message / reply | `chat.postMessage` | `channel`, `text`, `thread_ts`, `blocks`, `mrkdwn`, `reply_broadcast` | `chat:write` |
| Update message | `chat.update` | `channel`, `ts`, `text`/`blocks` | `chat:write` |
| Delete message | `chat.delete` | `channel`, `ts` | `chat:write` |
| List channels/DMs | `conversations.list` | `types`, `limit`, `cursor`, `exclude_archived` | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` |
| Get channel info | `conversations.info` | `channel` | `channels:read` |
| Read history | `conversations.history` | `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`, `latest` | `channels:history` |
| Find a channel by name | `conversations.list` + client filter | `types` | see conversations.list |
| Join channel | `conversations.join` | `channel` | `channels:join` |
| List workspace users | `users.list` | `limit`, `cursor` | `users:read` |
| Get user info | `users.info` | `user` | `users:read` |
| Get user by email | `users.lookupByEmail` | `email` | `users:read` |
| Open DM | `conversations.open` | `users` (comma-separated) | `im:write` |
| Search messages | `search.messages` | `query`, `count`, `cursor` | `search:read` |
| Upload file | `files.upload` | `channels`, `file` (multipart) or `content`, `filename` | `files:write` |
| List file comments etc. | `files.info` | `file` | `files:read` |
| Add emoji reaction | `reactions.add` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` | `reactions:write` |
| Set topic | `conversations.setTopic` | `channel`, `topic` | `channels:manage` |
| Create channel | `conversations.create` | `name`, `is_private` | `channels:manage` |
| Invite users | `conversations.invite` | `channel`, `users` | `channels:manage` |

Send parameters as `key=value` pairs. Use JSON-encoded values for arrays/objects, e.g. `blocks='[{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"hi"}}]'`.

## Channel names vs. IDs

- Most endpoints require a channel ID like `C1234567890`; channel names (`#general`) are accepted by `chat.postMessage` but not reliably by other endpoints.
- Resolve name → ID with `conversations.list` and match on `name` (public/private channels) or by inspecting `is_im`/`is_mpim` and users.
- `channels.conversations.list` returns both public and private channels when you pass `types=public_channel,private_channel`; include `mpim,im` for DMs.

## Timestamps

- Message `ts` values are strings like `"1717000000.000100"` — the seconds part alone is NOT a valid `ts`. Treat them as opaque strings and pass them back verbatim.
- `oldest`/`latest` filters accept Unix timestamps (seconds) or a `ts`-style string.

## Pagination

- List endpoints return at most 100–200 items per page (default 100) plus `response_metadata.next_cursor`.
- Repeat the request with `cursor=<next_cursor>` until `next_cursor` is empty to fetch all results.
- The bundled script does this automatically with `--paginate` and merges the result array.

## Rate limits

- Slack applies tiered rate limits, roughly 1 request/second per method per workspace for most methods (some like `auth.test` and `chat.postMessage` are higher).
- On throttling the API returns `"error": "ratelimited"` plus a `Retry-After` header (seconds). Wait and retry; back off on repeated failures.

## Error handling

Common errors and fixes:

| error | Meaning / fix |
|---|---|
| `invalid_auth` | Token invalid or revoked; refresh credentials. |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks permission; add the required scope (see catalog) or use a token with more scopes. |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot must be a member of the channel (`conversations.join`) or use `chat.postMessage` with a user token. |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad ID or bot not installed there; resolve the ID again. |
| `is_archived` | Channel archived; unarchive (`conversations.unarchive`) or pick another. |
| `ratelimited` | Too many requests; respect `Retry-After`. |
| `msg_too_long` | Text over 40,000 characters; shorten or use a file. |
| `restricted_action` / `access_denied` | Enterprise/admin policy blocks the action. |
| `not_authed` | No/invalid auth header present. |
| `account_inactive` | Token's user account is deactivated. |

Message payloads: a single message may combine `text` (fallback/plain) and `blocks` (rich layout). Keep `text` ≤ 40,000 chars; `blocks` ≤ 50 blocks.

# Slack Message Formatting (mrkdwn + Block Kit)

Table of contents:
- [Choosing text vs. blocks](#choosing-text-vs-blocks)
- [mrkdwn (plain messages)](#mrkdwn-plain-messages)
- [Block Kit](#block-kit)
- [Rules and limits](#rules-and-limits)

## Choosing text vs. blocks

- Simple announcements and alerts: use `text` with mrkdwn (`mrkdwn: true`).
- Rich layouts, buttons, or structured info: use `blocks` (Block Kit). Slack renders blocks when present and `text` is used as a fallback for notifications.
- Both can be combined in `chat.postMessage`: pass `text` for the notification and `blocks` for the in-channel layout.

## mrkdwn (plain messages)

Enable with `mrkdwn=true` (default in the web API when posting via `chat.postMessage`).

| You want | Write | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bold | `*bold*` | |
| Italic | `_italic_` | |
| Strike | `~strike~` | |
| Code | `` `inline` `` | |
| Code block | ```` ```code``` ```` | |
| Link | `<https://example.com|label>` | Without `|label`, URL shows raw |
| Mention user | `<@U123>` | Requires user ID, not `@name` |
| Mention channel | `<#C123>` | Requires channel ID |
| Mention group/everyone | `<!here>`, `<!channel>` | Use sparingly |
| Emoji | `:white_check_mark:` | |
| Quote block | `> quoted text` | Escape `>` in user content |

Escape user content: `&` → `&`, `<` → `<`, `>` → `>`. Never interpolate untrusted text unescaped.

## Block Kit

A message body is a JSON array of block objects. Most useful block types:

### Section (text + optional accessory)
```json
{"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Deploy complete* :rocket:"}}
```

### Section with fields (2-per-row layout)
```json
{"type": "section", "fields": [
  {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Status*\nSuccess"},
  {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Duration*\n4m 12s"}
]}
```

### Divider
```json
{"type": "divider"}
```

### Context (small helper text)
```json
{"type": "context", "elements": [{"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "By <@U123> · 2024-01-01"}]}
```

### Actions (buttons)
```json
{"type": "actions", "elements": [
  {"type": "button", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Approve"}, "style": "primary",
   "value": "approve", "action_id": "approve_btn"},
  {"type": "button", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Reject"}, "style": "danger",
   "value": "reject", "action_id": "reject_btn"}
]}
```

### Image
```json
{"type": "image", "image_url": "https://example.com/img.png",
 "alt_text": "screenshot", "title": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Result"}}
```

### Input (for modals/app surfaces, not channel messages)
```json
{"type": "input", "block_id": "reason", "label": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Reason"},
 "element": {"type": "plain_text_input", "action_id": "reason_input"}}
```

## Rules and limits

- ≤ 50 blocks per message.
- `text` fields in blocks: ≤ 3,000 chars each; `plain_text` may set `"emoji": true`.
- Buttons need a `value` or `url`; `action_id` identifies interactions.
- Replies in a thread: pass the parent message `ts` as `thread_ts`. To notify the whole channel from a thread reply, add `reply_broadcast=true`.

name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack API to send messages and thread replies, list conversations and users, read channel history, search messages, and upload files. Use when the user asks to post, fetch, search, or manage Slack messages, channels, users, reactions, or files, or to build Slack integrations with bot/user tokens or incoming webhooks.
---

# Slack API

Interact with Slack programmatically through the Slack Web API and incoming webhooks.

## Credentials

- Read the bot or user token from the environment variable `SLACK_TOKEN` (starts with `xoxb-` or `xoxp-`). If unset, look for a token in the project `.env` file, a credentials file, or ask the user.
- Use `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` for simple message posting when no token exists.
- Never hardcode, print, or log tokens. Prefer bot tokens with the narrowest scopes that work.

## Core workflow

1. Identify the destination. Most endpoints need channel/user IDs (`C123…`, `U123…`), not names. Resolve names first when the ID is unknown (see "Resolve a channel by name" below).
2. Choose the endpoint from [references/api.md](references/api.md) and check the required scopes.
3. Call the endpoint with the bundled script:

   ```bash
   python3 slack-api/scripts/slack_api.py <METHOD> key=value ...
   ```

   The script reads `SLACK_TOKEN`, posts to the Web API, prints one JSON result, and exits non-zero on failure. Use `--paginate` to follow cursors automatically.
4. Always inspect `"ok"`. If the response contains `"error"`, look it up in the error-handling table in [references/api.md](references/api.md) (`missing_scope`, `not_in_channel`, `ratelimited`, …) and fix the root cause rather than retrying blindly.

## Common operations

Send a message:

```bash
python3 slack-api/scripts/slack_api.py chat.postMessage channel=C123456789 text="Hello *world*!" mrkdwn=true
```

Reply in a thread (thread_ts is the parent message ts, as a string):

```bash
python3 slack-api/scripts/slack_api.py chat.postMessage channel=C123456789 thread_ts=1717000000.000100 text="+1"
```

Resolve a channel by name:

```bash
python3 slack-api/scripts/slack_api.py conversations.list types=public_channel,private_channel limit=200 --paginate
```

then match the returned objects on `name` and use their `id`.

Read recent history:

```bash
python3 slack-api/scripts/slack_api.py conversations.history channel=C123456789 limit=20
```

Search messages:

```bash
python3 slack-api/scripts/slack_api.py search.messages query="deploy failed" --paginate
```

Upload a file:

```bash
python3 slack-api/scripts/slack_api.py files.upload channels=C123456789 content="line1\nline2" filename=report.txt
```

Post to a webhook (no token needed):

```bash
SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/services/... python3 slack-api/scripts/slack_api.py webhook text="Deploy finished"
```

## Formatting messages

- For human-friendly announcements use mrkdwn (`*bold*`, `<@U123>` mentions, `:emoji:`) or Block Kit JSON for rich layouts with buttons and fields.
- Follow the patterns and limits in [references/formatting.md](references/formatting.md). Read it whenever composing user-facing message content.

## Rules and pitfalls

- Treat message `ts` values as opaque strings; pass them back verbatim. Never truncate or parse them as integers.
- Check `ok` on every response; HTTP 200 does not mean success.
- Respect Slack's rate limits (~1 request/second per method per workspace). Handle `"error": "ratelimited"` by waiting for the `Retry-After` value.
- Do not invent channel IDs or user IDs — resolve them from `conversations.list` / `users.list` when unsure.
- Verify the bot is a member of target channels (`not_in_channel` means it is not; join with `conversations.join` when the bot scope allows).
- Never echo credentials back to the user. Keep messages short and actionable.
